question: True or false: the 58°C measured at El Azizia, Libya, in 1922 is still the world's official hottest air temperature?
answer: False. A World Meteorological Organization panel rejected it in 2012 after 90 years in the record books: the observer was new to the job, the instrument was unsuitable, and the value was likely misread. The record passed to Death Valley's 56.7°C of 1913, a reading some meteorologists also doubt.
move: Long use makes a figure familiar; it does not make it verified.
ask: Which fact do I repeat only because I have always heard it, never because I checked it?
trap: Assuming a record that stood for 90 years must have been checked.
reference: El Fadli et al., World Meteorological Organization assessment of the purported world record 58°C temperature extreme at El Azizia, Libya, Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society, 2013
